description: Statutes and rules that interact with Civil Code § 1572 in California real estate fraud litigation.

refs.target: California Civil Code § 1567 (consent not free when obtained by fraud)
refs.relationship: § 1567 is the consent-invalidating statute; § 1572 is the definition of the fraud that invalidates consent. Both must be pleaded together when the plaintiff seeks rescission.

Separate from § 1572 actual fraud. § 1573 applies when there is a fiduciary relationship and a breach of duty without the specific intent element required by § 1572. A plaintiff may plead both in the alternative.

§ 1709 creates the tort of deceit; § 1710 defines the four kinds of deceit (substantially parallel to § 1572). The combination of § 1572 (contract fraud) and §§ 1709-1710 (tort deceit) allows plaintiffs to plead both contract rescission and tort damages.
Fraud under § 1572 is a triggering basis for punitive damages under § 3294 (clear-and-convincing-evidence standard). Every § 1572 complaint should also plead § 3294 to preserve punitive relief.

refs.target: California Civil Code § 3343 (real property fraud damages)
refs.relationship: § 3343 provides the out-of-pocket measure of damages for real property fraud. For § 1572 claims arising from real estate transactions, § 3343 controls the damages calculation (difference between price paid and actual value received), augmented by consequential damages.

refs.target: California Civil Code § 1102 et seq. (Transfer Disclosure Statement)
refs.relationship: § 1102 creates an affirmative statutory duty to disclose in residential real property transactions. Failure to comply with § 1102 can constitute suppression under § 1572(3) without any additional proof of duty.

§ 1100 governs which spouse has authority to dispose of community real property. A misrepresentation of authority to transfer community property is a § 1572(2) reckless assertion. § 1100(e) imposes fiduciary duty with affirmative disclosure obligation — parallel to § 1572(3).

refs.target: California Business & Professions Code § 10176 (real estate broker prohibited conduct)
refs.relationship: § 10176 enumerates misconduct grounds for broker license discipline, including fraud, substantial misrepresentation, false promise, and concealment. Every § 10176 violation is also a § 1572 civil claim.

refs.target: California Code of Civil Procedure § 338(d) (3-year statute of limitations for fraud)
refs.relationship: § 338(d) sets the SOL for fraud actions at three years from discovery of the facts constituting fraud. Discovery rule is critical — the 3-year clock runs from when plaintiff discovers or should have discovered the fraud, not from the date of the fraudulent act.

refs.target: Committee on Children's Television v. General Foods Corp. (1983) 35 Cal.3d 197
refs.relationship: Particularity-in-pleading rule for fraud claims. Every element of § 1572 must be pleaded with specificity (who, what, when, where, how). Conclusory fraud pleadings are subject to demurrer.

If the fraud is committed under color of state law (e.g., a court-supervised escrow or conservatorship transaction), the § 1572 claim may also support a § 1983 claim. Cross-reference to US Federal Civil Rights Litigator for the federal track.
